Consider the ellipse $E$ and the vector field $F,$ shown above. Let $C$ be any path where $E$ is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction. Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

III. ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$
question.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We now recall the following:

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false, while statement III is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves counterclockwise along $C.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14152067/assets/8595904122fac3431fc959b2fa4aa5a3062bd1bffd1a391a0861fa12f2498054.png)

So, ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

- Statement II is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves **clockwise** along $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14152067/assets/f1f31f2b6eefddedc46b8e845703904c0b4566963e64a644f7a4ab32bb7240c3.png)

So, ${∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
